source_name: CompanyWall MK — company financial/registry profiles for MK vendors
why_relevant: Registry-derived MK company profiles (observed for КаСис АД Скопје) giving incorporation date, address, and financial/employee indicators. Lets a supplier's headcount and revenue trajectory be validated independently of its own marketing — the quantitative backbone behind hiring signals, and a way to detect ownership or management changes.

source_name: Glassdoor — Skopje office pages & salary data for MK delivery centres
why_relevant: Per-company, per-location pages for the Skopje centres (G+D Netcetera, Nextsense observed) with salary points and review volume. Review-volume growth and salary drift are proxies for headcount growth and competition for payments engineers in Skopje.

source_name: Dun & Bradstreet business directory — MK vendor company profiles
why_relevant: Provides employee counts and revenue estimates per MK vendor entity (Nextsense d.o.o. Skopje observed at ~88 employees / ~USD 8.68m). Useful for sizing supplier delivery capacity and normalising hiring counts against base headcount.

source_name: Stopanska banka AD Skopje — e-banking installation/instructions and FAQ documents (supplier fingerprints)
why_relevant: Bank-published technical manuals and FAQs name the underlying components and trust providers (e.g. cooperation with KIBS as authorised issuer of digital certificates for MK), leaking the supplier stack that the private bank never discloses commercially. Same pattern applies across MK banks' PDF general-conditions and installation guides.

source_name: eCommerce Conference MK — Speakers Archive (AETM / Асоцијација за е-трговија на Македонија)
why_relevant: Annual regional e-commerce conference in Skopje (9th edition) with per-year speaker archive pages that state each speaker's exact title + employer. Historically includes bank payments executives (e.g. a Komercijalna Banka Cards and Current Accounts Department manager) and card processors (CaSys), plus NLB, Halk, Komercijalna, IUTE as sponsors. Year-over-year title drift between /2019/, /2020/, /2021/, /2022/ speaker archives is a direct read on silent promotions and unit renames in MK payments/cards teams.

source_name: Народна банка на РСМ (NBRNM) — conference & event pages incl. participant lists
why_relevant: The central bank hosts international research conferences, BSCEE annual conferences, payments/market-infrastructure conferences and HR-in-banking workshops, and publishes agenda and participant-list PDFs (a 'List of participants.pdf' for a Conference on Payments and Market Infrastructures was found under /content/Platni sistemi/). Participant lists name individual bank staff with their unit and title — an unusually granular org-chart proxy for both regulator and commercial banks.

source_name: MBA / Macedonian Banking Association LinkedIn page
why_relevant: Posts event photos and speaker credits naming bank executives with current titles; the follower/employee graph also exposes who works where. Highest-velocity channel for 'X spoke at Y as Head of Z' signals.

source_name: KIBS AD Skopje — corporate site and event/conference hosting (EACHA annual conference host)
why_relevant: Bank-owned clearing house and instant-payments operator; hosted the EACHA Annual Conference in Skopje (~200 participants from 30 countries). Its event communications name its own executives with exact titles (e.g. General Director Goran Anastasovski) and those of partner institutions, and its instant-payments licence milestones drive new unit/role creation — a reliable precursor to payments hiring.

source_name: EACHA (European Automated Clearing House Association) — annual conference agendas & speaker lists
why_relevant: EACHA's Skopje edition put MK payments leadership on an international agenda alongside their exact titles (EACHA president Jose Luis Langa; KIBS GD Goran Anastasovski; MBA president Maja Stevkova-Shteriev). Agendas of past/future editions list which MK institution sends whom, a cross-border check on MK payments org charts.

source_name: Balkan Payment Forum (ProMoney Events)
why_relevant: Regional payments forum (Tirana edition, ~25 speakers, 15+ regulators, 20+ countries) whose public speaker cards give name + exact title + institution, including MK-linked actors (e.g. the founder of Paysera Macedonia). Regional forums are where MK payments mid-leaders first appear publicly with a new title.

source_name: paytech.events — Fintech, Banking & Payments conference calendar
why_relevant: Aggregator calendar of banking/payments conferences; used to discover which regional events MK institutions attend or sponsor, and to enumerate new event sites for speaker-list harvesting. Pure pointer value, no MK-specific content of its own.

source_name: АБИТ — Академија за банкарство и информатичка технологија (ABIT Academy)
why_relevant: The first Macedonian banking academy (founded 2014), EBTN associate member, housed in the Macedonian Stock Exchange building; runs Certified Credit Analyst and other accredited specialisations and seminars, and has a strategic partnership with EFPA Luxembourg making Skopje a regional certification hub. Seminar/programme pages, lecturer rosters and news name practising bankers and their employers — a training-roster read on rising mid-level staff and on which skills banks are buying (a hiring leading indicator).

source_name: Finance Think — Institute for Economic Research and Policy, Skopje (economic forums, press conferences, webinars, team page)
why_relevant: Think tank whose Economic Forum, press-conference and webinar pages list panellists — typically ministry, central bank and commercial-bank economists — with current titles, and whose own 'Economic Team' page tracks the analyst bench that MK banks and the Ministry of Finance recruit from. Useful for spotting economist/analyst moves ahead of formal announcements.

source_name: Министерство за финансии — Annual Conference and seminars/training section
why_relevant: The Ministry of Finance runs an annual economic conference (e.g. 'Economic Recovery and Growth beyond COVID') with published programmes naming bank and regulator speakers by title, plus a standing seminars/training section. Agenda PDFs are a dated snapshot of who holds which public-finance and banking-supervision role.

source_name: MASIT — ICT Chamber of Commerce of North Macedonia (forums, summits, member directory)
why_relevant: Runs the Business ICT Forum / 'Digital Bridge' events with published agendas (downloadable PDFs) naming company executives; its member directory (including fintech-adjacent members such as Finelevate, Intertec, Aspekt) maps the vendor side of MK payments. Vendor executives moving into/out of bank technology roles show up here first, and event agendas timestamp their titles.

source_name: Macedonia2025 Summit — panels and speaker roster
why_relevant: Diaspora-backed flagship business summit in Skopje (e.g. 14 panels / 36 speakers, Skopje Marriott) mixing ministers, bank and fintech executives and think-tank directors. Panel line-ups are published with title+organisation and are a good annual snapshot of who is presented as the face of MK finance and digital policy.

source_name: Biznisvesti.mk — business media, conference and certification coverage
why_relevant: Carries MK finance-sector event and training news, including the ABIT–EFPA Luxembourg certification-hub story and EACHA/e-commerce conference speaker pieces. Useful discovery layer for awards, certifications and summits not indexed elsewhere.

source_name: The Banker / Global Finance — 'Bank of the Year' and 'Best Bank in Macedonia' award pages
why_relevant: The two award franchises that actually operate for North Macedonia (Komercijalna Banka repeatedly named Bank of the Year by The Banker and Best Bank in Macedonia by Global Finance). Award write-ups and acceptance coverage name the executives who collect the award and describe reorganised units — an indirect but dated read on who is in charge of what.

source_name: Економски факултет — Скопје (UKIM) — Chair of Finance, conferences, third-cycle conference
why_relevant: The main academic feeder for MK banking. The Chair of Finance staff page and the Monetary Economics / Finance and Banking programmes identify the academics who sit on bank supervisory boards and appear on conference panels; the international scientific conference ('Economic and Business Trends Shaping the Future') and the annual third-cycle conference publish programmes with affiliations. Also the recruiting pool signal for graduate hiring by banks.

source_name: Универзитет Американ Колеџ Скопје (UACS) — School of Business Economics & Management, news/events, internships
why_relevant: Private university with Finance and Banking programmes and an internationally ranked MBA; its news feed publishes corporate internship calls naming partner companies and departments (e.g. an internship in a Banking sector unit), guest-lecture and memorandum announcements, and faculty conference participation. Internship/guest-lecture partners are an early signal of which institutions are staffing up and which units exist.

source_name: ACAMS — North Macedonia country/term page and chapter events
why_relevant: ACAMS maintains a North Macedonia presence with local chapter meetups, training and CAMS certification. Chapter event pages and speaker credits name AML/compliance officers with their bank and title — a segment (compliance/financial crime) where MK banks hire heavily and where titles change quietly.

source_name: CFA Institute — 'Find a CFA Society' directory
why_relevant: Authoritative directory to determine whether a CFA Society exists for North Macedonia or whether MK charterholders affiliate to a neighbouring society (e.g. CFA Society Greece, which runs certificates/courses for the region). Determines where MK investment/treasury professionals surface publicly.

source_name: AI Tech Summit 'Filip Avramchev' (Skopje) — speaker roster
why_relevant: Recurring Skopje tech summit bringing global AI leaders; its programme/speaker page is where MK bank CTO/CDO-level and vendor-side people appear with current titles. Relevant to the payments-technology hiring signal; the konekt.mk piece is the pointer to the official summit site and its speakers section.

source_name: СФОМ — Синдикат на работниците од финансиските организации на Македонија (SFOM)
why_relevant: The single sector union organising bank, insurance, pension-fund and central-bank employees in North Macedonia. Its site carries the union statute, collective-agreement material, branch (синдикална организација) lists per bank and news of negotiations — the labour-side counterpart to bank restructuring, branch closures and headcount cuts. Member list observed on the site spans Komercijalna, NLB, Halkbank, Sparkasse, Silk Road Bank, Triglav, NBRSM.

source_name: ССМ — Сојуз на синдикатите на Македонија, грански синдикати
why_relevant: National confederation; its branch-union index is the authoritative pointer to which sector union covers financial-services workers and how it is named, plus links to each affiliate's own channel. Confederation news also carries general collective agreement (Општ колективен договор за стопанството) rounds that bind bank employers.

source_name: ССМ document archive (collective agreements, statutes)
why_relevant: Raw collective-agreement texts and union statutes hosted as DOC/PDF under a predictable path; useful for tracking the general economy-wide collective agreement text that frames bank-level agreements and redundancy procedures.
